Datasets: We adopt ten benchmark datasets across three reasoning tasks. Arithmetic: AQUA (Ling et al., 2017), GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021), SVAMP (Patel et al., 2021), MultiArith (Roy and Roth, 2015), AddSub (Hosseini et al., 2014), SingleEq (Koncel-Kedziorski et al., 2015b). Symbolic: Last Letters (Wei et al., 2024), Coin Flip (Wei et al., 2024). Commonsense: CSQA (Talmor et al., 2019), StrategyQA (Geva et al., 2021). Detailed statistics, including average difficulty and some parameters, are shown in Appendix D. Baselines: We compare with thirteen state-of-the-art (sota) methods, including five Zero-shot setting method: ZERO-SHOT, ZERO-SHOT-COT (Kojima et al., 2022), PS+ (Wang et al., 2023a), AUTO-COT (Zhang et al., 2023), COSP (Wan et al., 2023) Table 2: Main experimental results. Bold: the best score. Underline: the second best score. " -": not applicable.

and eight Few-shot setting methods: STANDARD (Brown et al., 2020), FEW-SHOT-COT (Wei et al., 2024), POT (Chen et al., 2022), COMPLEX-COT (Fu et al., 2023), SELF-ASK (Press et al., 2023), LEAST-TO-MOST (Zhou et al., 2023), SP (Xi et al., 2023), PHP (Zheng et al., 2023). More details are shown in Appendix E. Methods like SELF-CONSISTENCY (Wang et al., 2023b), DIV-SE and IDIV-SE (Naik et al., 2023) must generate multiple rationales then ensemble them, i.e., their settings are different from our method and all baselines. Hence, we follow all previous works to exclude them for fair comparison. Implementation details: For fair comparison, we adopt the gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 engine of GPT-3.5 for all methods in the main experiment. The only exception is PoT (Chen et al., 2022). We directly take its results since POt requires a codedavinci-002 engine, which is unavailable now. The temperature is set to 0 to ensure the stability and repeatability. We employ accuracy $(\%)$ as the metric. The demonstration set size $N$ for all datasets is set to 50 uniformly without further tuning. A parameter study for $N$ is given in section 4.6. The number of demonstrations $M$ for different datasets is consistent with previous methods (Zhang et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2024; Press et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2023; Xi et al., 2023; Zheng et al., 2023)

As mentioned in section 4.8, we investigate the time-consumption and token-consumption of different methods to explore computational efficiency. We compare our ADOT method with five best performing methods (PHP, FEW-SHOT-COT, LEAST-TO-MOST, SELF-ASK, COMPLEX-COT) in time-consumption. Closed-source LLMs (e.g., gpt-3.5-turbo-0613) cannot be downloaded, and interacting with them through API is susceptible to network conditions and other remote server-independent factors. To ensure a fair comparison, we investigate the time-consumption on the open-source LLMs 11ama2-7b-chat locally. All the experiments are done in the same environment on Nvidia A800 GPU. The comparison results on three tasks are shown in Fig. 7, which demonstrates that the time-consumption of our method is close to some simple methods (such as FEW-SHOT-COT) and much less than some complex methods (such as PHP). There are two main reasons for the less time consumption of our method. Frist, methods like PHP require iterative interaction with LLMs, while our method avoids this complex process. Second, the time-consumption is positively correlated with the length of input text. Our method only retrieves long demonstrations when the question is hard. However, the demonstrations of COMPLEX-COT and SELF-ASK are always long, so their time consumption is usually much longer than ours. From the perspective of token-consumption, we select three representative methods for comparison, including the previous best Zero-shot setting method COSP, the previous best Few-shot setting method PHP, and the vanilla chain-of-though pipeline FEW-SHOT-COT. The experimental results are shown in Table 6. Compared to FEWSHOT-COT, our method produces 62.91 additional tokens (on average of all datesets). Compared to the COSP and PHP methods, our method will reduce 310.7 and 17.6 additional tokens, respectively. Overall, our method improves reasoning performance and maintains high computational efficiency.
